narrative:
Your application was denied because the model places your chance of failing the bar exam on the first attempt at 72.5%. In plain terms, if you were admitted and took the exam, there is about a three-in-four chance you would not pass. That level of risk is what drove the decision.

The strongest factor in this forecast was your class standing in Year 3. You were in the bottom ten percent of your class, while admitted students on average are near the middle. This same pattern appeared in Year 1, where you were again in the bottom decile. These two factors alone told the model that you have struggled academically relative to your peers, and that this struggle strongly raises the risk of failing the bar.

Your undergraduate GPA was the third most important factor, but it worked in your favor. At 3.20, you are right around the average of admitted students, and a higher GPA generally pushes toward passing. However, the positive effect of your GPA was not enough to overcome the negative impact of your class rankings. Together, the rankings in Year 1 and Year 3 far outweighed the GPA advantage.

To improve your chances in the future, focus on raising your academic standing substantially. Consider strengthening your study skills, seeking academic support, or taking additional coursework that demonstrates your ability to perform at a higher level. If you reapply after showing a stronger record, the model may see a much lower risk of test failure.
